hardware_summary: Energos Winter (sole operating unit) runs steam turbine propulsion machinery; steam-turbine LNG carriers of this vintage use dual-fuel boilers that burn boil-off gas to raise steam for both propulsion and shipboard turbo-generators.
fuel_basis: Energos Infrastructure's own fleet page names Energos Winter's plant 'steam turbine propulsion' - the vessel was built by DSME as (per the operator) 'the second ever FSRU', an early Moss/steam-type LNG carrier conversion. Steam LNG carriers of this design class are dual-fuel-boiler vessels by construction (boiler burns boil-off gas plus bunker fuel; see Wikipedia's general LNG-carrier engineering description), so the plant is gas-capable; a vessel-specific boiler-fuel statement was not found despite search.
captive_summary: Damietta FSRU's sole unit, Energos Winter, is a moored former LNG-carrier FSRU on steam-turbine machinery. Steam LNG carriers of this class run dual-fuel boilers burning boil-off gas (as well as fuel oil) to generate the steam that (via turbo-generators, standard on this ship type) supplies the vessel's own electrical/hotel load and regas-plant power while moored - this is captive gas power under the FSRU-onboard convention. Confidence is yellow because the gas-burning capability is established by vessel-class engineering convention plus the operator's own 'steam turbine propulsion' label, not by a vessel-specific statement of boiler fuel.
confirmed_how: Energos's own fleet page (https://energosinfra.com/our_fleet/energos-winter/): 'Powered by steam turbine propulsion, Energos Winter enhances reliability and flexibility within Egypt's energy network' and 'the second ever FSRU', built by DSME. Wikipedia's general LNG-carrier article (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LNG_carrier): 'Normally, an LNG tanker is powered by steam turbines with dual fuel boilers that can run on methane... or bunker oil' and boil-off gas is 'traditionally diverted to the boilers and used as a fuel for the vessel' - general technical corroboration for the propulsion class, not vessel-specific.

fuel_basis: GE Frame 7 / Frame 7EA are gas turbines (combustion turbines fired on natural gas) - named explicitly as such by the plant's own technical paper, co-authored by SEGAS's Managing Director of Operations, Union Fenosa Gas's infrastructure director, and KBR/M.W. Kellogg (the FEED/EPC technology providers).
captive_summary: SEGAS's single LNG train (T1, operating) is driven by two GE Frame 7 gas turbines in the Split MRTM refrigerant-compressor configuration - classic mechanical-drive captive gas power, described in detail in the plant's own conference paper. This is a project-level finding and applies to the operating T1; T2 (shelved) was designed to the same configuration but never built. The paper separately references a distinct on-site 'power generation station'/'power generation units' as part of the plant's self-contained utilities, but does not state that unit's fuel - not needed for the verdict since the compressor-drive turbines alone already establish captive gas power via mechanical drive.
mechanical_drive_note: 2x GE Frame 7 (7EA) gas turbine drivers for the Split MRTM refrigerant compressors (one drives propane + HP MR compressors, the second drives LP/MP MR compressors), plus gas-turbine starter/helper motors; no MW/shaft-power rating stated in the source.
confirmed_how: GPA Europe conference paper 'Egypt's Premier LNG Project Establishes New Industry Benchmarks' (Fernández/SEGAS, Villanueva/Union Fenosa Gas, Mayer/M.W. Kellogg, Hill & Durr/KBR), https://www.gpaeurope.com/sites/default/files/download-file/documents/conference-papers/paper-6-MWK-LNG14-Segas.pdf: 'Split MRTM cycle with two Frame 7 gas turbine drivers, helper motors, and liquid expansion turbines' and '...using 2 GE Frame 7EA gas turbines as the primary drivers...
